text:
anya: seeing a surprising drop in prefix-cache hit rate after yesterday's quant+kernel rollout. hit % went from ~71% -> ~29% on the same traffic profile.
raj: wow that's huge. any quick diffs from the logs or cache key patterns?
anya: digging now. quick grep of cache keys from warmup buckets shows a bunch of keys differing only by trailing bytes.
anya: example (hex):\n  correct:  6f726967696e616c2d707265666978
  bad:      6f726967696e616c2d70726566697800
  so keys identical except an extra 00 at the end
mike: extra null byte appended? that smells like a tokenizer or padding change during tokenization/serialization after the kernel swap.
sophia: timeline check: we rolled quant profile v2 + fused-attn-layout on infra pool-3 at 03:12 UTC. tokenizer docker image was unchanged, but runtime now uses new padding path for matmul alignment.
anya: profiler snippet from a failed warmup run: \n  batch_size=8 seq=64 kernels=matmul_fp16_quantized
  prefix_cache_hits: 32
  prefix_cache_misses: 78
  observed_key_suffixes: ["\x00", "\x00\x00", ""]

raj: if padding is inserted at the RUNTIME step (post-tokenize) but keying happens pre-pad, mismatch could happen. Or vice versa.
mike: also saw this in a local repro: when we set align_to=512 in kernel config, TokenBuffer.pad_to multiple of 8 introduced binary padding on serialized key blob.
anya: reproduction steps I ran:\n  1) checkout runtime@fused-attn-rollout
  2) run ./tools/warmup_sim --model llama-13b --samples 10k --seq 64 --batch 8
  3) dump prefix keys to /tmp/keys.{good,bad}
  4) diff shows ~38% keys have trailing nulls in rollout build
sophia: can we canonicalize keys by trimming trailing \x00 when building cachekey? cheap fix and low risk.
raj: agreed as a short term mitigation. But we should be careful: some models/encoders might intentionally include 0 bytes in keys (edge case). Need to define canonical rule: strip trailing null bytes added purely by pad-to alignment. Add metadata tag indicating pad-mode and tokenizer-version to key to be robust.
mike: hotfix plan: key_canonicalizer:strip_trailing_nulls=true behind runtime flag + telemetry to measure effect. patch size ~20 LOC.
anya: also add extra telemetry: emit key_length_before/after and pad_mode for first 1M keys per pool so we can validate in prod without full perf hit.
deploy-bot: deploy recorded: rollout/fused-attn-layout -> pool-3 (started 2025-11-12T03:12:21Z)
anya: will push flag to pool-3 in canary (10%) then 100% if prefix-hit recovers. aim for canary today.
raj: longer term: move key generation to canonical text-based stable serializer (json-ish) + explicit pad meta to avoid binary surprises.
sophia: also add unit test covering token serializer + pad-to for different align_to values.
anya: quick numbers from my canary run with strip_trailing_nulls=true locally: hit rate goes back up ~68% and latency unchanged.
mike: ok sounds good. can someone open a PR with flag and tests? assign to me + anya.
anya: on it. I'll open PR + roll-canary playbook in #eng-oncall when ready.
raj: thanks everyone. let's keep an eye on KV eviction patterns after we change key lengths (might affect LRU distribution).\n
